newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan factions meet for U.N.-brokered peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Afghan factions meet for U.N.-brokered peace talks.

text.p: Feuding Afghan factions met in Islamabad under United Nations auspices on Monday to seek a ceasefire for war-ravaged Afghanistan, a U.N. official said.
The meeting, arranged by U.N. special envoy Norbert Holl, brought together three representatives of the Islamic Taleban militia and three from a northern opposition alliance.
The so-called working group last met in the Pakistani capital in mid-January with inconclusive results, though the two sides did agree to meet again in February.

The day after the January talks ended, the fundamentalist Islamic Taleban militia launched an offensive north of Kabul that eventually drove its opponents to the ramparts of the Hindu Kush mountain range.

Taking part in Tuesday's meeting were General Mohammad Paynda, representing northern General Abdul Rashid Dostum; Mohammad Ishaq, an aide to former government military chief Ahmad Shah Masood; and Mohammad Rasul Talib, from the Shi'ite Moslem Hezb-i-Wahdat faction led by Karim Khalili.
The names of the Taleban representatives were not immediately known.
The United Nations has been trying to persuade the rival groups to agree to a ceasefire, an exchange of prisoners and the formation of a technical committee to oversee the truce.
Success could lead to a dialogue on other issues such as the formation of a broad-based government, demilitarisation of Kabul and creation of a neutral security force for the city.

The Taleban have said in the past that they are ready for a ceasefire and prisoner exchange, but reject the idea of demilitarising Kabul. They also insist that any future government must rule in accordance with Islamic Sharia law.
The opposition has previously demanded agreement on the demilitarisation of Kabul as a condition for a ceasefire.
The Taleban, seeking to spread their purist vision of Islam across Afghanistan, hold most of the country after seizing Kabul on September 27 and deposing president Burhanuddin Rabbani.
